stimuli.title: Seven employees hold seven distinct ranks (rank 1 is junior-most and rank 7 is senior-most).
stimuli.body:
Clues:
1. Jatin is exactly 2 positions senior to Yuvraj.
2. Yuvraj is exactly 3 positions senior to Anika.

4. Firoz is immediately senior to Geeta.

stimuli.title: Seven candidates sit in a straight row, all facing north.
stimuli.body:

1. In the stated ordering, Zoya comes before Charu, and Charu comes before Priya.
2. In the stated ordering, Jai comes before Zoya, and Zoya comes before Om.
3. Om is at seat 4 from the left.

stimuli.title: Seven people live on different floors of a seven-storey building. Floor 1 is the bottom floor, and floor 7 is the top floor.

2. Vikram is exactly 2 positions above Varun.

stimuli.title: In a certain coded language, each word has one unique code.
stimuli.body:
violet mango feather = li ka ro
mango timber garden = fi zu ro
candle garden violet = ka zu no
feather candle timber = fi li no
stimuli.solution: mango=ro, violet=ka, feather=li, garden=zu, timber=fi, candle=no

questions.stem: Given the inequality chain Q = Z = V < U ≤ P, decide which conclusions follow. I: Q < Z. II: Q ≤ U.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: Exhaustive valid-order checking confirms: I is not necessarily true and II is always true.

questions.stem: Given the inequality chain Z = T < W = U > Q, decide which conclusions follow. I: U < Q. II: Z ≤ T.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: Exhaustive valid-order checking confirms: I is not necessarily true and II is always true.

questions.stem: Given the inequality chain W > S > V < U = X, decide which conclusions follow. I: W > V. II: V = U.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: Exhaustive valid-order checking confirms: I is always true and II is not necessarily true.

questions.stem: Given the inequality chain Z ≥ X > S > R > T, decide which conclusions follow. I: Z ≤ R. II: Z = X.

questions.stem: Given the inequality chain Z ≤ X ≤ Q < T > W, decide which conclusions follow. I: Z ≥ T. II: T > W.

questions.stem: Statements: No bakers are runners. Some runners are poets. Conclusions: I. Some poets are not bakers. II. No poets are bakers. Which conclusion follows?
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: The B∩C members are outside A; other C members remain unrestricted.

questions.stem: Statements: All singers are dancers. No dancers are drivers. Conclusions: I. No singers are drivers. II. Some singers are drivers. Which conclusion follows?
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: A is contained in B, while B and C are disjoint.

questions.stem: Statements: Some poets are sailors. No sailors are pilots. Conclusions: I. Some poets are not pilots. II. All poets are pilots. Which conclusion follows?
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: The A∩B members cannot be C.

questions.stem: Statements: Some coders are pilots. Some pilots are dancers. Conclusions: I. Some coders are dancers. II. Some pilots are coders. Which conclusion follows?
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: The two Some overlaps need not coincide; Some A are B converts to Some B are A.

questions.stem: Statements: All coders are runners. Some readers are coders. Conclusions: I. Some readers are runners. II. Some runners are readers. Which conclusion follows?
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: The existing C∩A members must lie in B, proving both conclusions.

questions.stem: Ritu walks 70 km north, then 56 km east, then 14 km south and finally 14 km west. What is her shortest distance from the starting point?
